commit a3b339198013a247587270899a02d0cdebc53d4f Author: John Bieling AuthorDate: Thu Oct 3 13:28:17 2024 +0300 Commit: John Bieling CommitDate: Thu Oct 3 13:28:17 2024 +0300 Bug 1918925 - Use x-ray vision only for known nested attachments. r=mkmelin jsmime uses a special format for the partName of a part of a nested message: `3$.2` This is addressing the 2nd attachment of an attached messages which itself is the 3rd attachment. Thunderbird is prettifying that partName to `1.3.1.2` in its message URLs. Before passing such a partName to jsmime, the prettified format was "decoded" again: ``` let partNum = partName.split(".").slice(1).join(".").replaceAll(".1.", "$.") ``` A hierarchy represented by a partName of the format `1.x.1.x...` was assumed to be always due to nested messages. However, that assumption was wrong. It is legal to have nested `multipart/*` parts which could generate such a partName without a nested message being involved. Forcefully "decoding" such a partName causes jsmime to not find the requested attachment, resulting in the reported bug. To fix this, we no longer auto-decode such partNames, but only when we know we want to access a nested attachment. We also add an additional parsing step, to see all parts returned by jsmime and match the one we are interested in. Nested attachments are not returned by listAttachments(). X-ray vision however was accessible through the WebExtension API by "guessing" the partName of a nested attachment. This allowed us to test x-ray vision. I would like to keep being able to do that, but since we no longer "auto-decode" nested partNames, the caller has to explicitly request x-ray vision by specifying a x-ray partName, for example `1.3$.2`. The schema definition was adjusted to allow such partNames to be used. That feature will remain undocumented.
